Finding things out

The change can be real. The detector can miss it.

A measuring tool can miss a change that another tool would reveal.

A closer lookOpen the shared interactive reader ↗

The interactive example has its own motion control. Scroll inside it if you need more room.

A result in a specified mathematical model

In the research example, one measurement gives the same answer while part of the mathematical system changes. Measuring several related quantities together can reveal more.

This works only if the measurements reach the changing part and are checked against a known reference. The research includes a computer experiment. A physical device would need its own tests.

Switch between the views. The added reference shows where each signal is in its cycle.

Words used here
calibration
Checking how a measuring tool’s readings relate to a known reference.
model
A simplified description used to explore a question. A result in the model needs further evidence before it describes the real world.
Read the fuller explanation

In the finite corpus example, one measured response stays unchanged while a hidden two-dimensional plane makes a quarter-turn. A calibrated matrix measurement can recover the moving projector.

The corpus develops this into a four-mode virtual instrument. Physical acquisition is a separate next step.

Where this comes from: What a measuring tool can see

Finite model result

A result in a specified mathematical model

One reading can miss a changing part of the model. Several well-chosen, checked measurements can reveal it. This is not yet a physical measurement.

Read the full source note

Scalar impedance and dark holonomy

In the finite witness, the scalar port e₄ is orthogonal to the moving dark plane. Its response is independent of the loop parameter. Full matrix residues recover the projector; a calibrated sufficiently ranked port set is needed experimentally.
